questions.q: The primary aim of the Food and Drugs Act (enforced by bodies like NAFDAC in Nigeria) is to...
options: ensure agricultural workers are paid a minimum living wage.
regulate the importation of heavy industrial machinery.
protect consumers from hazardous, fake, and unwholesome consumable products.
fix uniform market prices for all food items across the country.
questions.explain: The **Food and Drugs Act** is a core instrument of consumer protection. It strictly regulates the manufacture, advertisement, sale, and distribution of food, drugs, and cosmetics to ensure they are safe for human consumption and free from toxic substances.

questions.q: Which government legislation establishes an agency to verify that locally manufactured and imported industrial products meet minimum acceptable safety and quality specifications?
questions.explain: The **Standard Organisation Act** (which establishes the Standard Organisation of Nigeria - SON) is responsible for setting and enforcing minimum quality and safety standards for manufactured products (e.g., ensuring electrical cables are not substandard).

questions.q: The Price Control Act was historically enacted by the government primarily as a measure to...
options: prevent hoarding and arbitrary inflation of prices for essential commodities.
increase the cost of luxury imported goods like sports cars.
encourage sole proprietors to export more agricultural produce.
regulate the interest rates charged by commercial banks.
questions.explain: The **Price Control Act** is a government regulation tool used to fix the maximum retail prices of essential commodities. It aims to protect poor consumers from exploitation, arbitrary price hikes, and artificial scarcity caused by hoarding middlemen.

questions.q: The government legislation requiring employers to provide adequate ventilation, lighting, sanitary facilities, and first-aid equipment in the workplace is the...
questions.explain: The **Factory, Shops and Offices Act** is labour legislation specifically designed to mandate minimum standards for the health, safety, and welfare of workers in their respective places of employment.
